text:
ConocoPhillips edged up 0.23% today as oil prices held firm amid ongoing geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. A vessel strike in the Strait of Hormuz on September 13th kept crude elevated—U.S. oil at $97.26 and global oil at $109.51 per barrel—even as diplomatic signals (China pushing for BRICS-led peace, Indian appeals for dialogue) suggested some hope for de-escalation. For an oil company, higher crude prices directly support profitability, and the recent climb from $134.26 to $137.35 over the past week reflects this sustained elevation above $100 per barrel.

The stock has gained 6% in two weeks as the market weighs competing narratives: geopolitical risks that keep oil elevated versus diplomatic efforts that could eventually ease them. Trump's prediction of a sharp oil-price decline after midterm elections created volatility earlier in the week, but the Strait of Hormuz incident appears to have reminded investors that Middle East supply risks remain real and near-term.
